_meta.method: original literal English gloss from the Sanskrit commentary; Sanskrit order preserved; no machine-translation prose

1.translation: For my benefit you have spoken the supreme secret called spiritual teaching; by that word of Yours my delusion has departed.
word_for_word: for my benefit, for Your favor toward me

2.translation: I have heard from You in detail about the creation and dissolution of beings, O lotus-eyed one, and also about Your imperishable greatness.

3.translation: It is exactly as You say, O Supreme Lord. Yet I desire to see Your sovereign form, O Supreme Person.

4.translation: If You think it possible for me to see that form, O Lord, O Lord of Yoga, then reveal to me Your imperishable Self.

5.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Behold My forms, O Pārtha, by the hundreds and by the thousands—divine, of many kinds, and having many colors and forms. Though the form is one, Śrīdhara explains that the plural is used because of its manifold aspects.

6.translation: Behold in My body the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Aśvins, and the Maruts as well; behold many wondrous forms never seen before by you or by anyone else, O Bhārata.

7.translation: Behold here, gathered in one place within My body, the entire universe together with the moving and unmoving, O Guḍākeśa; and whatever else you desire to see, behold that also.
word_for_word: together with the moving and unmoving

8.translation: But you cannot see Me with these very physical eyes. I give you divine vision; behold My sovereign Yoga, My extraordinary power to bring about what is otherwise impossible.
word_for_word: you are able to see Me

9.translation: Sañjaya said: Having spoken thus, O King, Hari, the great Lord of Yoga, showed Pārtha the supreme sovereign form.

10.translation: It had many faces and eyes, many astonishing sights, many divine ornaments, and many divine weapons raised and ready.

11.translation: It wore divine garlands and garments, was anointed with divine fragrances, was made wholly of wonders, was radiant, endless, and had faces everywhere.

12.translation: If the radiance of a thousand suns were to arise simultaneously in the sky, it might perhaps resemble the radiance of that great Self.

13.translation: There Arjuna saw the entire universe, divided in many ways yet standing gathered in one place within the body of the God of gods.

14.translation: Then Dhanañjaya, filled with astonishment, his hairs standing on end, bowed his head to that God, joined his hands, and spoke.

15.translation: Arjuna said: O God, I see the gods in Your body, and likewise all the many groups of beings; Brahmā, the Lord, seated on the lotus seat; all the sages; and the divine serpents.
word_for_word: groups of distinct kinds of beings

16.translation: I see You with many arms, bellies, faces, and eyes, with endless forms everywhere. I see neither Your end, nor middle, nor beginning, O Lord of the universe, O Universal Form.
word_for_word: having many arms, bellies, faces, and eyes

17.translation: I see You crowned, bearing a mace and discus, a mass of radiance blazing on every side, difficult to behold, with the brilliance of blazing fire and the sun, immeasurable.
word_for_word: with the brilliance of blazing fire and the sun

18.translation: You are the imperishable, supreme Brahman to be known; You are the supreme support of this universe. You are the imperishable guardian of the eternal dharma; You are the eternal Person—this is my conviction of You.

19.translation: I see You without beginning, middle, or end, of infinite power, with infinite arms, with the moon and sun as Your eyes, with blazing fire as Your mouths, scorching this universe by Your own radiance.
word_for_word: with the moon and sun as eyes

20.translation: The space between heaven and earth, and all the directions, are pervaded by You alone. Seeing this wondrous and fierce form of Yours, the three worlds are greatly shaken, O Great Self.

21.translation: Indeed, these hosts of gods enter into You; some, terrified, praise You with joined hands. Saying “May there be well-being,” the hosts of great sages and perfected beings praise You with abundant hymns.
word_for_word: hosts of great sages and perfected beings

22.translation: The Rudras, Ādityas, Vasus, Sādhyas, Viśvedevas, the two Aśvins, the Maruts, and the Pitṛs who partake of the warm offering; the Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras, and hosts of perfected beings—all indeed look at You, astonished.
word_for_word: the Pitṛs who partake of the warm offering
hosts of Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras, and perfected beings

23.translation: Seeing Your great form, O Mighty-Armed One, with many faces and eyes, many arms, thighs, and feet, many bellies, and many terrifying tusks, all the worlds are shaken, and so am I.
word_for_word: with many arms, thighs, and feet

24.translation: Seeing You reaching the sky, blazing, many-colored, with gaping mouths and shining, immense eyes, my inner being is distressed; I find neither courage nor peace, O Viṣṇu.

25.translation: Seeing Your mouths, terrifying with tusks and resembling the fire of Time, I cannot recognize the directions and find no comfort. Be gracious, O Lord of gods, O Abode of the universe.
word_for_word: I do not know the directions

26.translation: All these sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with the hosts of earthly kings, and Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and that son of the charioteer, Karṇa, together with our principal warriors, are entering You.
word_for_word: the son of the charioteer, Karṇa

27.translation: They rush into Your terrifying mouths, dreadful with tusks; some are seen caught between the teeth, their heads crushed.

28.translation: As the many torrents of rivers flow toward the ocean alone, so these heroes of the human world enter Your mouths, blazing on every side.

29.translation: As moths, rushing with full speed, enter a blazing fire only for destruction, so these people also enter Your mouths with full speed only for destruction.

30.translation: You lick up and devour all the worlds on every side with Your blazing mouths. Your fierce radiances, filling the entire universe with their splendor, scorch it, O Viṣṇu.

31.translation: Tell me who You are, wearing this terrible form. Salutations to You, O best of the gods; be gracious. I desire to know You, the Primordial Person, distinctly, for I do not understand Your activity.

32.translation: The Blessed Lord said: I am Time, grown great, the destroyer of worlds, engaged here in bringing the worlds to their end. Even without you, none of the warriors stationed in the opposing armies will remain.
word_for_word: the maker of the destruction of worlds
to gather up or destroy the worlds
the warriors in the opposing armies

33.translation: Therefore arise, win fame, conquer the enemies, and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. They have already been slain by Me; become merely the instrument, O Savyasācin.

34.translation: Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Jayadratha, Karṇa, and many other heroic warriors have already been slain by Me; you slay them. Do not be distressed; fight, and you will certainly conquer your enemies in battle.

35.translation: Sañjaya said: Hearing this speech of Keśava, Kirīṭin, trembling, joined his hands, bowed to Kṛṣṇa, and again spoke, bowing down, in a voice choked with emotion, more frightened than before.

36.translation: Arjuna said: It is fitting, O Hṛṣīkeśa, that the universe rejoices and becomes attached through the praise of You; the frightened Rākṣasas flee in all directions, and all hosts of perfected beings bow to You.

37.translation: And why should they not bow to You, O Great Self, who are greater than Brahmā, the primal creator? O Infinite One, O Lord of gods, O Abode of the universe, You are the Imperishable, beyond the manifest and the unmanifest.

38.translation: You are the primal God, the ancient Person; You are the supreme support of this universe. You are the knower, the object to be known, and the supreme abode. O Infinite-Form, this universe is pervaded by You.

39.translation: You are Vāyu, Yama, Agni, Varuṇa, the moon, Prajāpati, and the great-grandfather. Salutations to You, salutations a thousand times; again and again, salutations to You.

40.translation: Salutations to You in front and behind; salutations to You on every side, O All. You are of infinite power and immeasurable might; therefore You pervade all things completely, and so You are all.

41.translation: Thinking of You as an ordinary friend, whatever I said rashly—“O Kṛṣṇa, O Yādava, O friend”—I ask You to forgive, whether from carelessness or affection, not knowing this greatness of Yours and this universal form.

42.translation: And whatever disrespect I showed You in jest during play, while lying down, sitting, or eating, whether alone, O Acyuta, or even in the presence of those friends, I ask You, the Immeasurable, to forgive all that.
word_for_word: during play, lying down, sitting, or eating

43.translation: You are the father of this moving and unmoving world; You are its worshipable one and its teacher, greater even than a teacher. None is equal to You, and who could be greater in the three worlds, O One of incomparable might?
word_for_word: of the moving and unmoving world
there is none equal to You

44.translation: Therefore, bowing and prostrating my body, I seek to please You, the Lord worthy of praise. O God, You should bear with my offense as a father bears with a son, as a friend with a friend, and as a beloved with the beloved.
word_for_word: having laid down the body, prostrating
I seek to please or propitiate
as a father with a son
as a friend with a friend
as a beloved with the beloved

45.translation: Seeing Your form never seen before, I am delighted; yet my mind is distressed by fear. Therefore show me that very familiar form, O God; be gracious, O Lord of gods, O Abode of the universe.

46.translation: I desire to see You as before, crowned, holding a mace and discus in Your hand. Become that very four-armed form, O Thousand-Armed One, O Universal Form.
word_for_word: holding a discus in the hand

47.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Because I was pleased, O Arjuna, I showed you this supreme form through My own Yoga—the luminous, universal, endless, primordial form of Mine that no one other than you has seen before.

48.translation: Neither by study of the Vedas and sacrificial lore, nor by gifts, nor by ritual acts, nor by severe austerities, can I in this form be seen in the human world by anyone other than you, O foremost of the Kurus.
word_for_word: not by study of the Vedas and sacrificial lore

49.translation: Let there be no distress or deluded state for you on seeing this terrible form of Mine. Free from fear and with a joyful mind, behold again this very form of Mine.
word_for_word: let there be no distress for you
and let there be no deluded state

50.translation: Sañjaya said: Having spoken thus to Arjuna, Vāsudeva again showed him His own former form and, becoming one with a gentle form, reassured that frightened one—the great and compassionate Lord.

51.translation: Arjuna said: Seeing this gentle human form of Yours, O Janārdana, I am now composed, conscious, and restored to my own natural state.

52.translation: The Blessed Lord said: This form of Mine that you have seen is exceedingly difficult to behold; even the gods always long to see this form.

53.translation: I cannot be seen in this form by the Vedas, austerity, gift-giving, or sacrifice, as you have seen Me.

54.translation: But through single-minded devotion alone can I, in this form, be known, seen in truth, and entered, O Arjuna, O scorcher of foes. Śrīdhara explains “entering” as entering through identity, not through another method.

55.translation: One who performs action for My sake, for whom I am the supreme goal, who is devoted to Me, free from attachment, and without enmity toward any being—such a person comes to Me, O Pāṇḍava.
word_for_word: having Me as the supreme goal
